animation_clip.doc:
A clip keys node properties over time. `length` is in seconds and may be
left out to end at the last key; `loop` is `none` (hold the last key),
`loop` or `pingpong`. Each track names a `target` node path relative to the
playing node (empty means that node), a `property` (`position`,
`rotation_euler`, `rotation`, `scale` or `<component>/<property>`), an
`interp` (`step`, `linear`, `cubic`) and its `keys`, each `{ t, value }` with
an optional `ease`. A track with no `property` is a method track whose keys
call the node's script. A file holds one clip, or several under
`[clips.<name>]`, addressed as `file.toml#name`.

```toml
type = "animation_clip"

[clips.patrol]
length = 4.0
loop = "pingpong"

[[clips.patrol.tracks]]
property = "position"
interp = "linear"
keys = [
  { t = 0.0, value = [-2.5, 0.25, -2.0] },
  { t = 4.0, value = [-2.5, 0.25, 2.0], ease = "in_out_sine" },
]
```

heightfield.doc:
A grid of heights for terrain: `rows` by `columns` samples in `heights`,
row-major, one value per grid point. The count has to match the grid.

```toml
[[assets]]
id = "valley"
type = "heightfield"
rows = 3
columns = 3
heights = [0, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
```

material.doc:
A shader and the values it draws with. `shader` names a `.wesl` file
(project-relative); `[features]` are the `@if` flags that pick a variant when
it is linked; `[params]` are the values of the shader's `Params` struct, by
field name. A number is an `f32`, an array of two, three or four numbers a
`vec2`/`vec3`/`vec4`, and a `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` string a `vec4`.

```toml
[[assets]]
id = "water"
type = "material"
shader = "shaders/water.wesl"
features = { lit = true }
params = { speed = 0.4, tint = "#3aa0ff" }
```

mesh.doc:
Geometry for `mesh`-typed properties. A definition either names a `source`
model file to import or carries the vertices itself as `positions` and
`indices`, which is what lets a script build one at run time; naming both is
refused. A `skin` table adds bone weights for skeletal animation.

```toml
[[assets]]
id = "blade"
type = "mesh"
source = "models/blade.obj"      # imported...
# ...or, instead of `source`:
positions = [[0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]]
indices = [[0, 1, 2]]
```

tileset.doc:
An image cut into equal tiles for the `tilemap` component: `texture` names
the image, `tile_size` is the pixel length of one tile edge and `columns` is
how many tiles one row of the image holds. Tile indices count row by row
from the top left.

```toml
[[assets]]
id = "dungeon"
type = "tileset"
texture = "art/dungeon.png"
tile_size = 16
columns = 8
```

voxels.doc:
A voxel grid for a collider: `size` is one cell in world units, `cells` the
filled coordinates. Coordinates are signed, so a grid has no origin corner,
and `physics3d.set_voxel` may add or remove a cell at run time.

```toml
[[assets]]
id = "pillar"
type = "voxels"
size = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
cells = [[0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 2, 0]]
```

widget_theme.doc: How each widget kind is drawn: `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke_width`, `radius` and `padding` under a table named for the kind (`[button]`, `[panel]`, `[row]`, ...). A kind the file leaves out keeps the built-in look. A widget takes the theme of the nearest ancestor that names one, so a screen is themed by its root.

component_docs.animation: Plays animation clips on a node: the library to play them from, one to start when the scene loads, and the rate every clip on the node runs at. The `animation` script module drives the playhead from there.
component_docs.body2d: Makes the node a 2D rigid body rapier simulates, in the xy plane: `dynamic` falls and responds to forces, `static` never moves, `kinematic` is moved by script or animation and pushes what it meets. Add a `collider2d` for it to collide with anything.
component_docs.body3d: Makes the node a 3D rigid body rapier simulates: `dynamic` falls and responds to forces, `static` never moves, `kinematic` is moved by script or animation and pushes what it meets. On its own a body has no shape; add a `collider3d` for it to collide with anything.
component_docs.bone2d: Makes the node a 2D bone: the rest position and rotation about z a rig returns to, plus the length and angle its gizmo is drawn with. A skin names its rig by node path and deforms by the bones under it, in tree order.
component_docs.bone3d: Makes the node a 3D bone: the rest position, euler rotation and scale a rig returns to, plus the length its gizmo is drawn with. A skinned mesh names its rig by node path and deforms by the bones under it, in tree order.
component_docs.camera: The view the scene is drawn from, following the node's global pose: `look_at` aims the 3D camera, `zoom` scales the 2D one in logical pixels per world unit. The last `current` camera of a kind, in tree order, drives that view.
component_docs.character2d: Moves a node the way a 2D player expects: `physics2d.move_character` slides it along walls, steps it up ledges, keeps it off slopes that are too steep and holds it to the ground over a crest. Needs a `collider2d`.
component_docs.character3d: Moves a node the way a player expects rather than the way physics would: `physics3d.move_character` slides it along walls, steps it up ledges, keeps it off slopes that are too steep and holds it to the ground over a crest. Needs a `collider3d`; a `body3d` of kind kinematic lets it push what it walks into.
component_docs.collider2d: The shape the node collides with in 2D. On a node with a `body2d` it is that body's shape; on a node without one it is immovable world geometry. A collider on a child node belongs to the nearest body above it, which is how one body carries several shapes.
component_docs.collider3d: The shape the node collides with in 3D. On a node with a `body3d` it is that body's shape; on a node without one it is immovable world geometry. A collider on a child node belongs to the nearest body above it, which is how one body carries several shapes.
component_docs.joint2d: Holds this node's body to another one in 2D: a hinge, a slider, a rope, a spring, or a generic joint you lock axis by axis. Both ends need a `body2d`.
component_docs.joint3d: Holds this node's body to another one: a hinge, a slider, a rope, a spring, a ball socket, or a generic joint you lock axis by axis. Both ends need a `body3d`.
component_docs.light2d: A 2D light: the node's position places it, its rotation aims a directional one, and everything drawn under it — sprites, polygons, tiles, a 3D scene behind them — is multiplied by the light map the scene's lights build. A scene with no `light2d` draws exactly as it does unlit; the first one added makes everything else fall to the camera's `ambient`. Debug lines and particles draw after the light map and stay unlit.
component_docs.listener: The ears a positional sound is heard from: its distance to this node sets its volume, and its offset across this node's right sets its pan. The last `current` listener applied wins; with no listener in the scene at all, every sound plays flat.
component_docs.mesh: Authored 3D geometry from a `mesh` asset, drawn at the node and deformed by the rig `skeleton` names when the asset carries a skin.
component_docs.modifier2d: Aims a 2D bone at a target node every frame, after the clip has posed the rig: `look_at` turns one bone toward the target, `two_bone_ik` bends a root, middle and tip chain so the tip reaches it.
component_docs.occluder2d: The outline this node blocks 2D light with. Left empty it follows the node's `collider2d`, or failing that its circle, capsule, rect or sprite shape, so the thing a player sees is the thing that casts the shadow. Every edge casts, so an occluder stands in its own shadow: a node that should stay lit wants a smaller outline or a light with `shadows = false`.
component_docs.particles: A purely visual 2D emitter at the node: rate, lifetime, speed, cone and gravity. The live particles and the randomness scattering them are backend state the simulation never sees.
component_docs.polygon: A filled, textured 2D polygon from a `mesh` asset's points and triangles, deformed by the rig `skeleton` names when the mesh carries skin weights.
component_docs.shape2d: An untextured 2D primitive drawn at the node -- circle, rect, capsule or a polyline traced through a mesh asset's points -- sized in world units.
component_docs.shape3d: An untextured 3D primitive drawn at the node -- ball, cuboid, capsule, cylinder, cone or plane -- sized in world units and tinted by `color`.
component_docs.sound: A sound of the node's own: which file, at what volume and pitch, looping or not. `audio.play_on` and `audio.stop_on` trigger it, and `autoplay` starts it when the node enters the scene. A `positional` sound is heard from where the node is, relative to the `listener`.
component_docs.sprite: A textured 2D quad at the node, sized from its image at `pixels_per_unit` texture pixels per world unit. A `columns` x `rows` sheet makes it a flipbook `frame` steps through.
component_docs.tilemap: A grid of tiles cut from one `tileset` atlas and centred on the node, one character per cell, drawn at `pixels_per_unit` tile-texture pixels per world unit.
component_docs.vehicle3d: Makes this node's body a car chassis, driven by the `wheel3d` children under it. Rapier casts a ray down from each wheel and pushes the chassis along a spring, which is how driving games model cars: it never jams and never tunnels.
component_docs.wheel3d: One wheel of the `vehicle3d` above it. Where the node sits on the chassis is where the wheel's ray starts; the rest is suspension tuning. Drive it with `physics3d.set_engine_force`, `set_brake` and `set_steering`.
component_docs.widget: A HUD element the widget layer draws every frame: a label, button or panel anchored to a screen corner or the center, offset in design pixels. A button records its click in `clicked` and calls the node's `on_click` method.

friction_slip.description: Grip along the wheel's rolling direction; lower slides more

max_force.description: The most force this suspension may push the chassis with

max_travel.description: How far the suspension may move in total

radius.description: The wheel's radius, which is how far off the ground it holds the ray's end

rest_length.description: How long the suspension is with no weight on it

side_friction.description: Grip sideways: what stops the car sliding out of a corner

stiffness.description: Spring stiffness: higher is a stiffer, twitchier car

align.description: Where a container puts its children across its own direction

anchor.description: Screen corner or center the offset is measured from

clicked.description: True on the frame the button was clicked

draw.description: What fills a `draw` widget: a script method on this node, or `scripts/file.rn:function` for a free function

focusable.description: Let focus land here. A widget nothing can activate is never focused whatever this says; set it false to skip one that could be

gap.description: Space between a container's children, in design pixels

grow.description: Share of the leftover space a container hands out along its own direction; 0 takes only what this widget asks for

height.description: Panel height in design pixels; 0 sizes to content

kind.description: The HUD element the widget layer draws

min_height.description: Smallest height a container may give this widget, in design pixels

min_width.description: Smallest width a container may give this widget, in design pixels

on_click.description: Script method called on this node when the button is clicked

on_focus.description: Script method called on this node when focus arrives

padding.description: Space inside a container's edge, in design pixels

text_key.description: A localization key drawn in place of `text`, re-read every frame so a locale switch shows at once

theme.description: How this widget and everything under it is drawn; inherited from the nearest ancestor that names one

visible.description: Draw the widget; hidden widgets keep their state

width.description: Panel width in design pixels; 0 sizes to content

x.description: Horizontal offset from the anchor, in design pixels

y.description: Vertical offset from the anchor, in design pixels

modules.doc: Clip playback on a node's `animation` component — starting, holding, seeking — and tweens, short clips generated from a table of steps and addressed by the handle they hand back.

docs.current: The clip playing or paused on this node, and nil once it has ended, been stopped, or never started.
docs.define: Give this node a clip of its own under that name, from a definition table shaped like a scene file's.
docs.is_playing: Whether a clip is advancing on this node; a paused, stopped, finished or absent one answers false.
docs.is_tween_running: Whether a handle still names a running tween; one that finished, was stopped, or lost its node answers false. Takes a tween handle, where `is_playing` takes a node and asks about its clip.
docs.just_finished: The clip that ended on this node during the last step, and nil on every other frame.
docs.pause: Hold the playhead where it is, keeping the clip current so `resume` has something to go back to.
docs.play: Start the clip of that name on this node; the trailing options table takes `speed` (a multiplier) and `from_start`.
docs.queue: Play the clip of that name once the current one ends; a looping clip never ends, so a queue behind one never drains.
docs.resume: Carry on from where `pause` left off; a stopped, finished or never-started node is left alone.
docs.seek: Move the playhead to a number of seconds and pose the node there, even on a paused or ended clip.
docs.stop: End the clip on a node, or the tween a handle names, leaving the pose where it is; `resume` cannot revive it.
docs.time: Seconds of playback since the current clip started, before wrapping; a stopped clip keeps where it stopped.
docs.tween: Generate a clip on the node from a table of steps and run it, returning the handle `stop` and `is_tween_running` take.
docs.tween_to: Move one property of the node to a value over a number of seconds on an optional easing curve, returning a handle.

modules.name: animation

modules.doc: Apple platform services that `platform.*` does not cover. `identity` fetches what a server needs to verify a Game Center player — url, signature, salt and timestamp — and answers on a later tick as a map carrying `kind`, both to the node's `on_apple` method and to whoever awaits the id. Achievements, leaderboards, sign-in and cloud saves are `platform.*`, which speaks Game Center here.

docs.authenticated: Whether Game Center has a signed-in player right now.
docs.available: Whether this build has Apple's frameworks behind it.
docs.cancel_notification: Drop a scheduled notification, and take a delivered one out of the shade.
docs.credential_state: Ask whether a saved Sign in with Apple account is still authorized, revoked, transferred or unknown.
docs.entitlements: What this player currently owns, each with the signed transaction a server checks.
docs.finish_purchase: Tell StoreKit a transaction is dealt with. One that is never finished comes back on every launch.
docs.identity: Fetch the items a server needs to verify this Game Center player, and return the id the answer carries.
docs.notify: Schedule a local notification. The options take `title`, `after` in seconds and an `id` to cancel or recognise it by.
docs.products: Ask the App Store about a list of product ids, and answer with what it knows: title, description, price and display price.
docs.purchase: Buy a product. The answer is `purchased`, `cancelled` or `pending`, and a purchase carries the signed `jws` a server checks.
docs.register_for_push: Ask the OS for a push token. It arrives at everything watching, not at the caller, because the OS hands it over whenever it likes.
docs.request_notifications: Ask the player to allow notifications, and answer with what they said.
docs.restore_purchases: Ask the App Store to hand this device's purchases back — the button a review expects a game to have.
docs.sign_in: Sign in with Apple, and return the id the identity token comes back on. Game Center's own sign-in is `platform.sign_in`.
docs.watch: Subscribe a node's method to everything that arrives unasked: a notification tapped, a URL opened, a push token, a transaction that landed elsewhere.
docs.watch_urls: Hear about URLs the game is asked to open while it runs. A URL the game was launched with arrives before the engine boots and is not one of them.

modules.name: apple

modules.doc: Asset definitions by reference: a project-relative file path, `file#entry` for one entry inside it, or `#id` for a block the scene declares. A script gets the definition table, not the parsed object the owning plugin builds from it.

docs.directory: The project-relative directory files of an asset type belong in; empty when the type is unknown or declared none.
docs.duplicate: A private copy of a definition, read past the cache, so editing it disturbs no other holder of that reference.
docs.exists: Whether a reference resolves to a definition that is really there; false rather than an error when it does not.
docs.invalidate: Declare everything derived from project files stale — a shader a material links, say — so it is rebuilt from disk; for a file the watcher does not cover.
docs.load: The definition table behind a reference, from the cache; an error when the reference resolves to nothing.
docs.reload: Forget a reference so the next load re-reads its file, along with every entry cut from that same file.
docs.save: Write a definition table to the project-relative file a reference names; an error unless it names a whole file.

modules.name: assets

modules.doc: Sound playback: a file plays under an integer handle, with `volume`, `pitch` and `loop` options, and the `sound` component gives a node a sound of its own. Give a `play` a `position` and it is heard from where the `listener` is. With no output device every call still works and nothing is heard.

docs.bus_volume: One bus's own gain, without its parents'.
docs.buses: Every audio bus, declared in `[audio.buses]` or made by setting a volume, in name order.
docs.distance_gain: The gain the distance to the listener is costing a positional handle right now: 1 up close, 0 out of range.
docs.emitter_position: Where a handle played with a `position` is; nil for a flat or unknown one.
docs.events: Every sound named in `audio/events.toml`, in name order.
docs.is_playing: Whether a handle's sound is still audible; false once it ends, and always false with no output device.
docs.listener: Where the ears are: the current `listener` node's world position, or what `set_listener` last put there.
docs.pan: Where a positional handle sits between the speakers: -1 hard left, 0 centred, 1 hard right.
docs.play: Start the audio file at a path and return the handle `stop`, `set_volume`, `set_pitch` and `is_playing` take. The options table takes `volume`, `pitch`, `loop`, `bus`, and a `position` with `min_distance`, `max_distance` and `doppler`.
docs.play_event: Play a named sound: the next of its variations in turn, at its own volume and pitch, through its own bus. A `position` in the options table places it. Nil for a name nothing declared.
docs.play_on: Start the node's own `sound` from the top, replacing what it had going, and return the new handle.
docs.set_bus_volume: Set one bus's gain and re-apply it to everything already playing on it — which is what a volume slider is.
docs.set_emitter_position: Move what a handle plays from, so a sound follows something the script is driving; the frame takes its doppler from how far it moved.
docs.set_listener: Put the ears at a point by hand, for a game whose view is not a node; a `listener` node in the scene takes it back on the next frame.
docs.set_pitch: Set a playing handle's speed multiplier, which carries its pitch with it.
docs.set_volume: Set a playing handle's linear gain, where 1 is the file's own level.
docs.stop: Silence the sound a handle names; a finished, stopped or unknown handle is left alone.
docs.stop_all: Silence everything at once and clear the playback every `sound` component was holding.
docs.stop_on: Silence what the node's `sound` started; a node carrying none is left alone.

modules.name: audio

modules.doc: Breakpoints, the pause a stopped script sits in, and the ways out of it. The same machinery the editor's Debugger dock and the Debug Adapter Protocol server drive, so an outside editor and the built-in one see one debugger.

docs.break_on_error: Whether a script that throws stops rather than being logged.
docs.breakpoints: The lines one file's breakpoints landed on.
docs.paused: Where a script is stopped — node, path, line, reason and frames, innermost first — or nil while none is.
docs.request_break: Ask to stop at the next line any script runs; nothing is stopped yet when it returns.
docs.resume: Let the stopped script go on, in the given step mode (`CONTINUE`, `STEP_OVER`, `STEP_INTO`, `STEP_OUT`).
docs.scope: The node whose subtree a pause holds still, or nil when a pause stops the whole tree.
docs.set_break_on_error: Stop where a script throws instead of logging it and moving on; off by default.
docs.set_breakpoints: Replace one file's breakpoints with the given lines, returning the lines they landed on.
docs.set_scope: Limit the pause to one node's subtree, so an editor keeps running while the game stops; nil means the whole tree.

modules.name: debugger

modules.doc: The running app itself: the clock a frame reads, the command line it was started with, the directory it may write to, and the way out.

docs.args: The command-line arguments the app was started with, empty when it was given none.
docs.delta: Seconds the frame in progress covers, the same number a system is handed.
docs.quit: Ask the app to shut down; the frame in flight still finishes.
docs.reload_script: Recompile one script by its project-relative key, for a tool editing files outside the watched root.
docs.tick: Which frame this is, counted whole — what simulation code branches on instead of `time`.
docs.time: Seconds of engine time since the app started, accumulated as a float.
docs.timings: What the last frame cost, in seconds: `{ frame, fixed_steps, stages, spans }`. Presentation only — branching a `fixed_update` on wall time desyncs, and nothing records it.
docs.user_data_dir: A writable per-user directory for saves and settings, created on first call and named after the project.

modules.name: engine

modules.doc: Files on disk, project-relative unless the path is absolute, so a script cannot wander the filesystem by accident. This is the disk itself: a packed build's contents are reached through `assets` and `scene.source`.

docs.exists: Whether a project-relative path has anything at it, file or directory.
docs.list: A directory's entries as `{ name, is_dir }`, sorted, dotfiles skipped; empty for a directory that is not there.
docs.mkdir: Create a project-relative directory and every parent it needs.
docs.mtime: When a file last changed, in seconds since the Unix epoch; nil for one that is not there.
docs.read: A whole file as text, project-relative unless absolute; nil when it cannot be read.
docs.remove: Delete a project-relative file, or a directory and everything under it; false when there was nothing there.
docs.rename: Move a project-relative file or directory, creating the destination's parent first.
docs.write: Write text to a project-relative file, creating the directory it goes in.

modules.name: fs

modules.doc: The Gamend backend: a session, its REST API, and a realtime socket carrying topics and server hooks. Every call returns an id to await, and each result also reaches the handler method of the node it was given (`on_gamend_event` unless `on_event` names another) as a map tagged with a `kind`.

docs.call_hook: Call a server plugin's function over the socket; the reply's `response` holds `data` or `error`.
docs.close: Shut the socket down; false when the connection was already gone.
docs.configure: Point the plugin at a server's base url; every other call errors until this one runs.
docs.connect: Open the realtime socket and return the id `join`, `push`, `leave`, `call_hook` and `close` take.
docs.join: Subscribe the socket to a topic and return the id the server's `reply` answers.
docs.leave: Unsubscribe the socket from a topic, returning the id the `reply` answers.
docs.login: Open a session from a `device_id`, or an `email` and `password`, and return the id its `login` result answers.
docs.push: Send an event and its payload to a topic on the socket, returning the id the `reply` answers.
docs.rest: Call a path on the configured server over HTTP; the result carries the `status` and the decoded `body`.

modules.name: gamend

modules.doc: Mesh operations that stand outside the simulation: hulls, convex decomposition, voxelisation, cutting and boolean intersection. A mesh is an asset's name or a table of `points` and `indices`.

docs.convex_decomposition: The mesh cut into convex pieces, each one a mesh: the only way to collide a concave shape dynamically.
docs.convex_hull: The tightest convex shape containing every point: what a dynamic collider wants when the model is concave.
docs.intersect: The mesh both meshes have in common, or nothing when they do not overlap.
docs.pieces: The mesh's separate parts, one mesh each: what a model that was already broken is made of.
docs.split: Cut the mesh with a plane, returning the two halves: `#{ point = [..], normal = [..] }`.
docs.voxelize: The mesh as a voxel grid — `#{ size, cells }`, ready to be a `voxels` asset — so a model can become destructible terrain.

modules.name: geometry3d

modules.doc: HTTP calls, off the frame: the reply arrives on a later tick as a map with `status`, `headers` and `body`, or with `error`, both to the node's `on_response` method and to whoever awaits the returned id. Options are `method`, `headers`, `body` and a `timeout` in seconds, which falls back to the project's `[http] timeout`.

docs.request: Start an HTTP request and return the id its reply carries, to await or to match inside the handler.

modules.name: http

modules.doc: One frame of input: the keyboard, mouse, touch screen and gamepads as they stand now, plus the edges — what went down or came up this frame. Nothing feeds it in a headless run, where every query answers neutrally rather than failing.

docs.action_just_pressed: Whether the action went down this frame.
docs.action_just_released: Whether the action came up this frame.
docs.action_pressed: Whether the action is held down now.
docs.action_value: How far the action is pushed, -1 to 1; a key answers 0 or 1, a stick or `keys:A,D` the whole range.
docs.actions: Every action `[input.actions]` declares, so a rebinding screen can list them.
docs.bind: Rebind the action to one binding or a list of them, replacing what it had and saving to the user data directory.
docs.bindings: What the action is bound to now, whether from the project or from the player's own rebinding.
docs.declare_actions: Declare the actions a project's `[input.actions]` would, from a table of name to binding list; for a host running a project other than its own, such as the editor.
docs.dropped_files: The absolute paths of files dropped onto the window this frame, in drop order; desktop only.
docs.feed_key: Press or release a `KEY_*` key as if the window had reported it; the edge lasts this frame, the state until the opposite feed.
docs.feed_mouse: Move the cursor to a window-pixel position as if the window had reported it; the delta accumulates for this frame.
docs.feed_mouse_button: Press or release a `MOUSE_*` button as if the window had reported it.
docs.gamepad_acceleration: The pad's acceleration in g, gravity included, so a pad at rest reads 1 on one axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no accelerometer.
docs.gamepad_axis: How far the pad's `AXIS_*` stick or trigger is pushed, -1 to 1; zero at rest and for an absent pad.
docs.gamepad_can_rumble: Whether the pad has motors to rumble; false for a pad that is not connected, and on a build with no force feedback.
docs.gamepad_down: Whether the pad's `PAD_*` button is held down right now, however many frames it has been down.
docs.gamepad_gyro: How fast the pad is turning, in radians per second about each axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no gyroscope.
docs.gamepad_just_pressed: Whether the pad's `PAD_*` button went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.gamepad_just_released: Whether the pad's `PAD_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.gamepad_name: The pad's name as the platform reports it, empty when no pad has that id.
docs.gamepad_rumble: Rumble the pad, `{ strong, weak, duration }` — the two motors at 0..1 for that many seconds. Returns whether it started; a second rumble replaces the first.
docs.gamepad_stop_rumble: Silence the pad now, rather than waiting out the rumble's duration.
docs.gamepad_touches: Every finger on the pad's touchpad as `{ id, x, y }`, oldest first, with x and y running 0 to 1 across the surface. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; empty for a pad with no touchpad.
docs.gamepads: The ids of every connected pad, ordered so the list is stable from frame to frame.
docs.is_down: Whether the `KEY_*` key is held down right now, however many frames it has been down.
docs.is_mouse_down: Whether the `MOUSE_*` button is held down right now, however many frames it has been down.
docs.just_pressed: Whether the `KEY_*` key went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.just_released: Whether the `KEY_*` key came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_delta: How far the cursor moved this frame, in pixels; movement, not a position.
docs.mouse_just_pressed: Whether the `MOUSE_*` button went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_just_released: Whether the `MOUSE_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_position: The cursor's position in window pixels, with (0, 0) at the top-left corner.
docs.reset_bindings: Drop every saved rebinding and go back to what the project declared.
docs.scroll_delta: How far the wheel turned this frame, as an (x, y) pair; zero when it did not turn.
docs.touches: Every finger on the screen as `{ id, x, y }`, oldest first, in the same pixels as `mouse_position`.
docs.touches_ended: The ids of the fingers that lifted or were cancelled this frame.
docs.touches_started: The ids of the fingers that touched down this frame.
docs.typed: The characters typed this frame, in order: what a text field appends, where `just_pressed` says which key went down.

modules.doc: JSON text to and from script values, for talking to anything outside the engine. Unlike TOML it has null, so nil survives a round trip.

docs.encode: A value written back out as JSON text; NaN, infinity, a node or a callback has no JSON form and is an error.
docs.parse: The value a JSON document describes; an error on text that does not parse.

modules.name: json

modules.doc: The three levels a script writes at, and the buffer behind them. Scripted lines go through the engine's own `tracing` stream, so they land beside engine ones.

docs.clear: Empty the buffer, so a console reading it starts again from nothing.
docs.error: Write a line at error level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.info: Write a line at info level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.recent: The last n buffered entries, 100 by default, each `{ time, level, tag, message, fields }`.
docs.warn: Write a line at warning level, tagged as coming from a script.

modules.name: log

modules.doc: Deterministic float maths, backed by pure-Rust `libm`: the same inputs give the same bits on every platform. A script uses these rather than the language's own float methods, which reach for the platform's libm and drift between machines.

docs.abs: The magnitude, with the sign dropped.
docs.acos: The angle in radians whose cosine is the argument, from 0 to PI; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.asin: The angle in radians whose sine is the argument, from -PI/2 to PI/2; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.atan: The angle in radians whose tangent is the argument; with two arguments, the y-then-x form instead.
docs.atan2: The angle in radians from the positive x axis to the point, taking y first and x second.
docs.ceil: The smallest whole number at or above the argument, still a float.
docs.clamp: The first argument held inside the range given by the second (low) and third (high).
docs.cos: The cosine of an angle in radians.
docs.exp: e raised to the given power.
docs.floor: The largest whole number at or below the argument, still a float.
docs.log: The natural logarithm, or the logarithm in the base given as a second argument.
docs.log10: The base-10 logarithm; -INF at zero and NaN below it.
docs.pow: The first argument raised to the power of the second.
docs.round: The nearest whole number, with halfway cases going away from zero.
docs.sin: The sine of an angle in radians.
docs.sqrt: The square root; NaN for a negative argument.
docs.tan: The tangent of an angle in radians.

modules.name: math

modules.doc: What every node has: its name and path, its transform in local and world space, its children, its components and its script. Each operation takes the node as its first argument, so scripts normally call them as methods on a node value (`this.node.position()`).

docs.add_child: Create a named child node under this one and return it.
docs.attach_script: Attach the script at a path, with an optional table overriding what the script exports.
docs.call: Call a method on the node's script and return what it gives back; nil when there is no such script or method.
docs.children: The node's direct children, an empty list when it has none.
docs.component_names: The names of every component on the node.
docs.detach_script: Drop the script instance on this node, so no further lifecycle call reaches it; the node and its components stay.
docs.get_component: The named component's properties as a table, nil when the node does not carry it.
docs.get_node: The node at an `A/B/C` path relative to this one, `..` climbing to the parent; nil when nothing matches.
docs.global_position: The node's position in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_rotation_euler: The node's world rotation as euler angles in radians, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_scale: The node's scale in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.has_component: Whether the node carries the named component.
docs.is_valid: Whether the node is still in the world; false rather than an error when the value is not a node.
docs.name: The node's own name, empty when it carries none.
docs.parent: The node's parent, nil at the root.
docs.path: The node's slash-separated path, built by climbing parents from the node up to the root.
docs.position: The node's position in its parent's space.
docs.queue_free: Destroy the node and its subtree at the end of the frame.
docs.remove_component: Take the named component off the node.
docs.rotation_degrees: The same local rotation as `rotation_euler`, in degrees.
docs.rotation_euler: The node's local rotation as euler angles in radians, x then y then z.
docs.scale: The node's scale relative to its parent.
docs.script_path: The path of the script attached to the node, nil when it has none.
docs.set_component: Give the node the named component, built from the given table over the component's schema defaults.
docs.set_name: Rename the node, doing nothing when it carries no name.
docs.set_parent: Move the node under another, keeping where it is in the world; an error for a cycle or a dead parent.
docs.set_position: Move the node to a local position, given as three numbers or one vector.
docs.set_rotation_degrees: Set the node's local rotation from euler angles in degrees.
docs.set_rotation_euler: Set the node's local rotation from euler angles in radians.
docs.set_scale: Set the node's scale relative to its parent, as three numbers or one vector.
docs.translate: Move the node by an offset in its parent's space, given as three numbers or one vector.

modules.name: node

modules.doc: What spans both physics worlds at once: pausing, sleeping and clearing. Bodies and colliders live in `physics2d` and `physics3d`.

docs.clear: Remove every body and collider from both worlds, as a play-in-editor session does on stop.
docs.counters: What the last step spent its time on. Zeroes unless the engine was built with rapier's profiler.
docs.debug_draw: What the debug renderer is drawing now, as a table of `enabled` and one flag per mode.
docs.quarantined: The nodes rapier disabled this step because their position or velocity stopped being a number. Empty is the normal answer.
docs.set_debug_draw: Draw the physics world over the scene: `true` for the usual shapes, or a table naming modes (`#{ colliders = true, joints = true }`).
docs.set_paused: Stop or resume stepping both worlds; nodes keep their poses.
docs.set_sleeping_allowed: Allow or forbid resting bodies falling asleep, in both worlds and for bodies added later.
docs.set_threads: How many threads rapier's solver may use. Only a build with the `parallel` feature has any; on a serial build this says so and changes nothing.
docs.set_tuning: Change how the solver behaves in both worlds: `solver_iterations`, `length_unit`, `ccd_substeps`, contact softness and the rest. Every value here changes results, so a recording only replays against the same numbers — prefer `[physics]` in project.toml.
docs.sleeping_allowed: Whether resting bodies are allowed to fall asleep.
docs.threads: How many threads the solver is using; 1 on a serial build.
docs.tuning: The solver settings both worlds are running with.

modules.name: physics

modules.doc: The 2D rigid-body world: bodies and colliders on nodes, their velocities, and overlap queries. `physics` holds what spans both worlds.

docs.add_body: Give the node a 2D rigid body of the given kind (`BODY_DYNAMIC`, `BODY_STATIC`, `BODY_KINEMATIC`).
docs.add_collider: Attach a 2D collider from a `collider2d` table: `kind`, `radius`, `half_extents`, `friction`, and the rest of the component's own vocabulary.
docs.add_force: Push the body until the force is reset; unlike an impulse this is spread over time.
docs.add_force_at_point: Push at a world point, which also turns the body.
docs.add_joint: Tie this node's body to another with a 2D joint, from a `joint2d` table.
docs.add_torque: Turn the body until the torque is reset.
docs.angular_velocity: How fast the body is spinning, in radians per second.
docs.apply_impulse: Add an instant change in momentum, as if the body were struck.
docs.apply_impulse_at_point: Strike the body at a world point, which spins it as well as moves it.
docs.apply_torque_impulse: Add an instant change in angular momentum, as if the body were spun.
docs.body_kind: Whether the body is dynamic, static, kinematic or kinematic_velocity.
docs.box_hits: Every collider whose bounds meet an axis-aligned box.
docs.damping: This body's linear and angular damping.
docs.distance: The gap between two nodes' colliders, zero when they touch.
docs.intersects: Whether two nodes' colliders overlap right now, sensor or not.
docs.is_ccd: Whether continuous collision detection is on for this body.
docs.is_enabled: Whether the body is being simulated.
docs.is_grounded: Whether the last move ended with ground under the character's feet.
docs.is_sleeping: Whether the body is asleep and being skipped.
docs.joint_impulse: How hard the joint is pulling right now.
docs.kinetic_energy: The body's kinetic energy, for a rest test the solver agrees with.
docs.linear_velocity: How fast the body is travelling, in units per second.
docs.locked_axes: Whether x, y and rotation are frozen.
docs.mass: The body's total mass, colliders included.
docs.max_contact_impulse: The hardest contact this body took in the last step, zero when nothing touched it.
docs.move_character: Move the character by an offset, sliding along walls, climbing steps and staying on the ground: returns `#{ x, y, grounded, sliding, collisions }`. Call it from fixed_update.
docs.nearest_point: The closest point on any collider to a world point.
docs.next_position: The position a kinematic body has been told to move to.

modules.doc: Record what a running game is fed and play it back. A recording holds each tick's input, network arrivals and events, not the world they produced, so a session is small and replays by re-running the game against the same input. docs.marks: The ticks at which one replay source held a non-empty list under a key, and what it held.

modules.doc: The engine's one deterministic PCG32 stream: the same seed draws the same numbers on every platform, and a replay reproduces every draw a recorded session made.

modules.doc: Rollback netcode from a script's side. The session decides each tick's inputs before the tick runs — the real one where it has arrived, a repeat of the player's last one where it has not — and `input` reads whichever it settled on. A tick may run more than once: when a late input contradicts a prediction, the engine restores the tick before it and simulates forward again, so anything a script does with an effect outside the simulation has to ask `is_resimulating` first.

docs.input: What that player is doing on the tick being simulated, real or predicted; nil outside a session or for a player it does not know.
docs.is_resimulating: Whether this tick is a re-run of one already simulated, so a script can skip anything it must not do twice.

docs.set_widget_layer: Turn drawing of the scene's `widget` nodes on or off, and confine it to an x/y/w/h rect in design pixels.
docs.shortcut: Whether this chord was pressed this frame, consuming it; `mods` is `"cmd+shift"`, from the `MOD_*` constants.
docs.slider: Draw a horizontal slider between `min` and `max`; returns the value after this frame and whether it moved.
docs.spacing: Set the gap between the current container's widgets, in design pixels.
docs.text_field: Draw a single-line text box keyed by `id`; returns its text, whether it changed, and whether Enter was pressed.
docs.toggle: Draw an on/off switch; returns the state after this frame and whether it was clicked.
docs.top_panel: Dock a strip across the top of the window and draw the callback inside it; `height` is in design pixels. Answers the height it ended up with.
docs.vertical: Lay the callback's widgets out in a column.
docs.wants_keyboard: Whether a UI widget holds keyboard focus, so the game should leave this frame's key presses alone.
docs.window: Draw the callback in a floating window the user drags and resizes; false once its close button is used.

modules.doc: A long-lived connection carrying text or binary frames. Its events are a stream, not a result: each one reaches the connecting node's handler method (`on_websocket_event` unless `on_event` names another) as a map `{ socket, kind, .. }` with kind `open`, `message` (with `text`), `binary` (with `bytes`), `closed` or `error`, and nothing awaits a socket id.

docs.close: Ask the connection to close, which still delivers a `closed` event; false when it was already gone.
docs.connect: Open a connection and return the id `send` and `close` take; options are `on_event`, `compression` and `headers`.
docs.send: Queue a frame on the connection, text for a string and binary for bytes; false when it is already gone.
